How a nearest-neighbour read of several sources is served.

dot-mosaic_read_spec.Rd

Tiles no mosaic VRT can hold (south-up tiles, tiles in a neighbouring projection, one Zarr array per UTM zone) stay a multi-path source. A nearest-neighbour read of it takes each target cell from one source pixel, a later source winning where it holds data, so the sources can be read one at a time and laid over each window in order (gdal_read_window_multi()): a direct window read where a source lies on the target's pixels (.rio_direct_spec(), partial = TRUE), and elsewhere an exact nearest-neighbour warp of that source alone, clipped to its footprint. Only the sources off the target's pixels pay for warping, and the cells are those the warper gives all the sources together.

Usage

.mosaic_read_spec(paths, target_grid, band = 1L, nodata = numeric(0))

Arguments

paths

The source paths, in mosaic order.

target_grid

The WarpNode target GridSpec().

band

1-based band index (or indices) the read will use. Their data types drive the integer gate above.

nodata

The source node's sentinel (length 0 or 1). Averaging declines unless the file declares the same value.

Value

NULL (the warper reads them together), or a list with fx = fy = 1, resamp, the target grid and parts, one a source: its .rio_direct_spec() result, or list(warp = TRUE), each with box, its footprint in target pixels c(c0, r0, c1, r1).

Details

Float sources whose nodata is not NaN keep the warper when any two overlap: it lets a later source's NaN value cover an earlier source's data, which a paste that skips NaN cannot tell from nodata. Memoised per sources (and their local file stamps), target, bands and nodata.
